newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest air cargo import delays to end - Malev.
newsitem.headline: Budapest air cargo import delays to end - Malev.

text.p: Ferihegy Airport in Budapest plans by Friday to end delays from new customs regulations in releasing imported cargo, Hungarian national airline Malev Rt said on Thursday.

"The delays will be eliminated tonight," Ferenc Kovacs, Malev's cargo manager, told Reuters. "Cargo arriving on planes this afternoon will not be subject to backlogs when business resumes on Friday morning."

Imported goods have waited as long as five days for customs clearance since September 30, when regulations took effect to improve the tracking of cargo movements within Hungary, airport officials said.

The new rules slowed clearance procedures by creating additional paperwork, including documents requiring customs to register goods transferred between the warehouses of the airport's two cargo handlers -- Malev and the air traffic and airport authority LRI -- airline and airport officials said.
Delays occurred because most imported cargo must be transferred between the warehouses, a process that required no paperwork before the rules took effect, the officials said.
Transfers often are necessary because Malev handles most airlines, while most freight forwarders have offices at LRI's warehouse, airport officials said.
Customs officials responded to the delays by deciding on Wednesday to waive the paperwork required for the transfer of cargo from Malev's warehouse to LRI's warehouse, Kovacs said.
"LRI gained a general authorisation on Wednesday from the customs office at the airport to receive cargo arriving at our warehouse for LRI customers and freight forwarders," he said.
Customs and LRI officials were not available for comment.
Airlines said they expect the authorisation to be valid until customs offices at the airport are equipped to handle the new regulations efficiently.
The offices recently received additional computers and staff to manage the extra paperwork, and a new system to register cargo will be installed in January to prevent future delays, LRI said earlier.
Malev is owned 30 percent by Italian airline Alitalia.
